name: v0.9.74
body:
- Feature: four more language extractors gained structural depth. **Ruby** paren-less self-sends (`do_thing` with no receiver or parens) are now captured as calls, with a local-variable/parameter/block-parameter in scope correctly suppressing the call (fail-closed, no fabrication) (#3960, thanks @rajatnagda45). **TypeScript** `abstract` method signatures in an abstract class are now extracted as callable method members and resolve as call targets (#3961, thanks @rajatnagda45). **Scala** deferred (abstract) method declarations in traits and abstract classes (`def foo: Int`, no body) are now extracted as methods (#3962, thanks @rajatnagda45). **C++** a member-function declaration inside a class (`void foo();`, defined out-of-line) is now classified as a method rather than a field, including pure-virtual, `const`, operator, and destructor forms; real data members stay fields (#3963, thanks @rajatnagda45).
- Fix: a Rust type used before it is declared in the same file now resolves to its local declaration instead of fabricating an external stub; resolution is a two-pass, order-independent scan, and a forward reference whose name collides with another same-id item is kept unresolved (fail-closed) (#3903, #3782, thanks @Yyunozor).
- Fix: Rust prelude types (`Option`, `Result`, `Vec`, `String`, `Box`, `Rc`, `Arc`, `HashMap`, and friends) no longer accumulate spurious in-degree and surface as god nodes that distort community detection and ranking; they are filtered at extraction time, and a type the file defines itself is kept. Tuple-struct and unit-struct construction (`ClientId(id)`) is reclassified from a `calls` edge to a `references`/`constructor` edge (#3973, thanks @liam-mcelhaney122).
- Fix: an Obsidian-style wikilink to a note whose name contains a dot (`[[v1.2 release]]`, `[[note.en]]`) now resolves instead of being dropped by a premature extension strip; plain, explicit-extension, anchor, and alias wikilinks are unchanged, a literal indexed file beside the link keeps precedence, and a genuinely missing target is still not fabricated (#3905, #3904, thanks @Yyunozor).
- Fix: a constructor call whose target is a same-file annotation stub (a source-less node minted by an earlier annotation or generic-argument reference) is kept for cross-file resolution and binds to the real definition when there is import or namespace/using-scope evidence, instead of being dropped; a genuinely external unresolved name is still not fabricated (#3901, thanks @bercedev).
- Fix: the CLI hook-guard that protects graphify's own output directory now resolves paths and checks real containment instead of substring matching, so a sibling directory sharing a name prefix (`artifacts/graphify-notes` vs `artifacts/graphify`) is no longer wrongly treated as inside the output dir; symlinks, `..`, relative paths, and case-insensitive filesystems are handled (#3964, #3959, thanks @shobhitagnihotri69).
- Fix: when resolving an import of a workspace package that ships both a source entry and a built dist, the graph now prefers the source file (so edges point at authored code) and falls back to the built artifact only when no source entry exists, generalizing the existing source-over-dist preference from the `exports` path to the legacy `main`/`module` fields (#4000, #3834, thanks @Adityakk9031).
- Feature: Verilog header files (`.vh`) are now detected and extracted through the same tree-sitter-verilog grammar as `.v`/`.sv`, so macros, parameters, and modules declared in headers are captured (#3983, thanks @oleksii-tumanov).
- Fix: an incremental update no longer drops a hyperedge from an untouched file when a re-extracted file emits a hyperedge with the same id; carried hyperedges are now keyed by `(id, source_file)` so a same-id edge from a different, unchanged file is preserved while a genuine same-file re-emit still replaces (#3997, #3981, thanks @Ayushraj06-bit).
- Feature: Kotlin class-literal references in annotation arguments (`@ManyToOne(targetEntity = Customer::class)`) are now extracted as attribute references to the referenced type (#3965, #3835, thanks @hopstreax).
- Fix: Lua colon-method calls (`obj:method()`, `self:method()`) now resolve to the table-qualified method definition; a non-`self` receiver fails closed with no cross-file member fabrication (#3994, thanks @rajatnagda45).
- Feature: Erlang local fun references (`fun Name/Arity`, as in `lists:map(fun helper/1, L)`) are now recorded as `indirect_call` edges to the arity-matched local function; remote `fun Mod:Name/Arity` and anonymous funs are left as-is, and an undefined or arity-mismatched local fails closed (#3996, thanks @rajatnagda45).
- Fix: C# null-conditional member calls (`receiver?.Method()`) now resolve through the same typed-receiver path as `receiver.Method()`, including the call-site generic-argument walk; chained and element-access forms fall through to bare-name resolution with no fabrication (#3976, #3797, thanks @Cintu07).

body:
# Cua Driver 0.33.0

## Summary

This release adds 2 features and includes 17 fixes.

## Features

- auto-link skills for Pi. ([#4049](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/4049)) Thanks @kvnloo; reported by @tyxlb.
- let embedding hosts set the macOS key gap. ([#3489](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/3489)) Thanks @hyprcat.

## Fixes

- accept verbatim and junctioned Windows browser installs. ([#4467](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/4467)) Thanks @qtqjcz.
- validate Windows capture handles. ([#4333](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/4333)) Thanks @AnvitDevadiga; reported by @ART1KZ.
- support rotated Hyprland outputs. ([#3969](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/3969)) Thanks @osamahbeig.

## Contributors

Thanks to @0xsline, @AnvitDevadiga, @ART1KZ, @biztex, @Ed-Key, @Feighery89, @hyprcat, @Iflaqbhat, @kvnloo, @lorenzozanee, @muness, @nothingtolose09-sys, @osamahbeig, @qtqjcz, @tyxlb for contributing to this release.

## Install

macOS and Linux:

```bash
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://cua.ai/driver/install.sh)"
```

Windows:

```powershell
irm https://cua.ai/driver/install.ps1 | iex
```

Cua Driver ships universal macOS binaries, x86_64 and arm64 Windows builds,
and Linux preview builds. Release assets also include tag-pinned installer and
uninstaller scripts.

## Why GitHub says “Pre-release”

GitHub's label is used only to keep this monorepo's repository-wide “Latest”
pointer from switching between independently released products. A plain Cua
Driver SemVer is a stable release; npm and PyPI publish it on
their normal stable channels, and the installers resolve the versioned
`cua-driver-rs-v*` releases directly.

name: Windows Terminal Preview v1.26.2734.0
body:
We're coming out of our long Summer (northern hemisphere) hibernation to bring you a new Preview release of Windows Terminal: 1.26! We've been hard at work on the Settings page, workspaces, notifications, and general fit _and_ finish. Lots more community contributions this time around (thank you to all of you!) and _many_ of the bug fixes you see here have been backported to 1.25 and--in some cases--1.24!

## Features

* This release includes our newly-redesigned settings UI! Broadly, the categories are the same, but we've given a new interface to most of our settings, simplified wording, moved things into logical groups, and more. Profiles is probably the biggest difference, where we've moved all of the profile tabs, color schemes and the Defaults section into one top-level "Profiles" area (#20232) (#20743) (#20336) (#20665) (#20200) (#20658) (#20646) (#20215) (#20199)
* We have added early support for "workspaces," or named Terminal windows which remember what was open in them that you can close and come back to. Access Workspaces with the new icon to the left of the tab list (#20314) (#20663)
* We now support applications emitting a notification with OSC 777 (Desktop Notification, from urxvt) and additionally support for displaying a notification when a bell is triggered. Please note that both of these behaviors are *off by default*, and require you to opt in to enable them. JSON settings `$profile`.`compatibility.allowOSC777` (boolean) and `$profile`.`bellStyle` enum value `notification` (#20012) (#20018) (#20011) (#20064) (#20010)
* The "confirm closing tabs" setting has been redesigned to prompt any time you are going to close more than one thing, prompt always or prompt never (#20055)

## Changes

* `wt --help` will try to be more clear about how unrecognized arguments are handled (#20417) (thanks @ManyaS-Git!)
* Duplicating a tab will now unconditionally open it to the right of the source tab (#20565) (thanks @OmarMashal0!)
* On newer versions of Windows, Terminal will use faster APIs to query the app catalog to find fragment extensions (#20356)
* Our build system now requires Visual Studio 2026 and Windows SDK 10.0.26100 (#20225) (#20518) (#20609)
* Panes can no longer be reduced below 2 cells in either direction, to prevent screen corruption (#20564) (thanks @zhangxaochen!)
* Tab Search will now "preview" which tab you are about to jump to while you're searching (#20256)
* Terminal will now cause DWM.exe to use less memory per Terminal window! (#20655) (thanks @YexuanXiao!)
* The "Open New Window" action has been improved to make it impervious to app execution alias failures (i.e. `wt.exe` being corrupted) (#20311)
* The console will no longer emit `WINDOW_EVENT` events when a VT application enters or leaves the Alternate Screen Buffer (#20617)
* The info bar exhorting you to please not disable the "Touch, Keyboard, and Handwriting Input Service" has been removed (#20633)
* The soft reset (`DECSTR`) control sequence now works like xterm does when the alternate screen buffer is in use (#20032) (thanks @aarushisingh04!)
* The support for `OSC 7` which was announced in version 1.25, and then removed, has likewise been removed from 1.26
* We are rolling out runtime changes to improve our code quality; however, that rollout is currently restricted to the Dev channel (local builds) (#20544)
* We got rid of the "new tab" animation, as it made the application appear slower (#20543)
* We have expanded our "built-in glyph" support to cover a large portion of the new Unicode "Symbols for Legacy Computing" block (we now cover `U+1FB00` through `U+1FB94`, all sextants, filled triangles and trapezoids, and eighth blocks) (#20424)
* We have laid the groundwork for "per-window settings", which in the future will allow you to specify a different theme, profile, etc. for each Window or Workspace (#20328)
* We have made some changes under the hood to prepare for merging our "Terminal control" codebases (#20713) (#20711) (#20722) (#20017)
* We have renamed the (somewhat confusing, probably) "New Tab Menu" settings page to "Dropdown", and redesigned it to be (somewhat, maybe) easier to use (#20203)
* We will now show an overlay indicating the size in character cells of the window when you resize Terminal (#20059) (thanks @sagarbhure-msft!)
* When you close a tab, Terminal will now unconditionally jump to the previously most recently used tab (#20272) (thanks @Anshikakalpana!)
* You can now customize what delimiter is used when you drop multiple files on a Terminal pane; JSON setting `dragDropDelimiter` (string, default is a single U+0020 space) (#19799) (thanks @Vallabh-1504!)

## Bug Fixes

* IME candidate windows will no longer be positioned incorrectly when Terminal is maximized (#20627) (thanks @9enki!)
* Terminal will no longer send arrow key inputs (and others) in the middle of an IME composition (#20471) (thanks @sanguneo!)
* Custom shaders which depend on the `time` parameter will no longer experience an early rollover (#20360) (thanks @Zish19!)
* A completely empty terminal pane or console window will no longer try to commit the first 128 rows of the buffer to memory (#19984)
* Errors displayed in the Settings page will now be more visible in high contrast mode (#20098) (thanks @SushaanthSrinivasan!)
* Media paths referring to icon resources such as `foo.exe,-1` will once again work (#20572) (thanks @arista-ms!)
* Terminal should no longer leak memory with some graphics adapters when you are scrolled back into history or experience rendering lag after the machine resumes from sleep (#20723)
* Terminal will no longer stay open indefinitely with no windows open if it has been asked to host an incoming session that terminated early (#20051) (thanks @Kuldeep2822k!)
* The "action name" input field will no longer try to convince you that you hadn't changed anything (#20455)
* The "Open Current Working Directory" action will no longer attempt to open non-directories (#20697) (thanks @SebTardif!)
* The font face selector in the settings UI will no longer cause Terminal to undergo rapid unscheduled disassembly (#20255) (thanks @danyalahmed1995!)
   * ... it will also no longer instantly forget what you put in it (#20359) (thanks @danyalahmed1995!)
* The JSON settings schema has been updated to include `persistedLayoutAndContent` as a valid option for `firstWindowPreference` (#20475) (thanks @doterik!)
* We now use a lighter-weight API to play sounds when "bell sounds" are enabled (#20031) (thanks @aarushisingh04!)
* We now use the most recent Azure Cloud Shell API version, which ensures that you can still access your Cloud Shells (#20620) (thanks @mbifeld!)
* We've fixed some visual artifacts experienced by users of the "QQ Wubi" IME (#20542)

### Reliability

* XBOX controllers will no longer cause Terminal to shuffle off this mortal coil (#20234) (thanks @phil-scott-78!)
* We will take fewer trips to a farm upstate when you use "terminal pane" shortcuts on the Settings, Markdown or Snippets UI (#20458)
* The experimental "reposition mouse cursor with click" settings will now result in fewer "bucket-kicking" events (#20442)

### VT Support

* An application initiating an OSC 52 clipboard write at the same time as a title change will no longer experience a 5-second hang (#20728)
* A VT soft reset (DECSTR) will no longer result in the uploaded soft font (DRCS) being cleared (#20607) (thanks @j4james!)
* Kitty Keyboard Protocol: auto-repeat events now work properly (#20500)
* Kitty Keyboard Protocol: dead keys and numpad Enter now work properly (#20551)
* Kitty Keyboard Protocol: non-ASCII keys, modifier repeats and AltGr keys now work properly (#20052)

### Console Hosting

* ConPTY will no longer retry its cursor position request when the hosting application does not answer it (#20510)
* ConPTY will no longer wait for a DA1 response before finishing initialization (#20536)

## Miscellaneous (console host, build systems, code health)
* conhost: headless console applications no longer spawn a useless render thread (#19986)
* conhost: we now always use the "cls" detector to prevent screen clearing from committing the entire (virtualized) text buffer (#19957)
* Our release engineering process now supports uploading our NuGet packages to GitHub (#20061)
* The "restart session" menu item on each tab will now be disabled if there is no session to restart (#19972)
* We've streamlined how we handle word-wise selection and navigation; this should result in no user-facing issues but :shrug: (#19882)

With additional documentation, build system, schema, and code health fixes thanks to @tusharsnx, @MichaelK05-dev, @BamBamTram32, @slambek, @raza-khan0108, @nsfxdyj, @DinahK-2SO, @nsfxdyj, @winstliu, and @1816586742-stack.

---

_Binary files inside the unpackaged distribution archive bear the version number `1.26.260930004-preview`._

name: Windows Terminal v1.25.2733.0

* A rich "actions" editor that will let you better customize how you interact with Terminal.
* Support for the "Kitty" input protocol, for a highly opinionated way to distinguish keyboard keys and how they were pressed.
* Window persistence with _or without_ the scrollback history.
* Community translations into Ukrainian and Serbian (Cyrillic).

* Kitty Keyboard Protocol: auto-repeat events now work properly (#20500)
* Kitty Keyboard Protocol: dead keys and numpad Enter now work properly (#20551)
* Kitty Keyboard Protocol: non-ASCII keys, modifier repeats and AltGr keys now work properly (#20052)

### Console Hosting

* ConPTY will no longer retry its cursor position request when the hosting application does not answer it (#20510)
* ConPTY will no longer wait for a DA1 response before finishing initialization (#20536)

With additional documentation, build system, schema, and code health fixes thanks to @tusharsnx, @MichaelK05-dev, @BamBamTram32, @slambek, @raza-khan0108, @nsfxdyj, @DinahK-2SO, @nsfxdyj, @winstliu, and @1816586742-stack.

name: Windows Terminal v1.24.12741.0
body:
While Terminal 1.25 is slowly rolling out (as we get new reliability info, prove it doesn't super-explode, etc.), we've decided to update 1.24 with a couple quick fixes as well to make sure you're not left out in the cold.

## Changes

* Panes can no longer be reduced below 2 cells in either direction, to prevent screen corruption (#20564) (thanks @zhangxaochen!)
* We got rid of the "new tab" animation, as it made the application appear slower (#20543)

## Bug Fixes

* IME candidate windows will no longer be positioned incorrectly when Terminal is maximized (#20627) (thanks @9enki!)
* Terminal will no longer send arrow key inputs (and others) in the middle of an IME composition (#20471) (thanks @sanguneo!)
* Media paths referring to icon resources such as `foo.exe,-1` will once again work (#20572) (thanks @arista-ms!)
* The font face selector in the settings UI will no longer cause Terminal to undergo rapid unscheduled disassembly (#20255) (thanks @danyalahmed1995!)
   * ... it will also no longer instantly forget what you put in it (#20359) (thanks @danyalahmed1995!)
* The JSON settings schema has been updated to include `persistedLayoutAndContent` as a valid option for `firstWindowPreference` (#20475) (thanks @doterik!)
* We now use the most recent Azure Cloud Shell API version, which ensures that you can still access your Cloud Shells (#20620) (thanks @mbifeld!)
* We've fixed some visual artifacts experienced by users of the "QQ Wubi" IME (#20542)

### Reliability

* XBOX controllers will no longer cause Terminal to shuffle off this mortal coil (#20234) (thanks @phil-scott-78!)
* We will take fewer trips to a farm upstate when you use "terminal pane" shortcuts on the Settings, Markdown or Snippets UI (#20458)
* The experimental "reposition mouse cursor with click" settings will now result in fewer "bucket-kicking" events (#20442)

### VT Support

* An application initiating an OSC 52 clipboard write at the same time as a title change will no longer experience a 5-second hang (#20728)

name: v1.4.219
body:
Thank you so much for using Orca and for your continued support! ❤️

This patch is built from the September 30 daily build plus fixes picked from main. Pull requests that landed on main after that are not in this build.

## The short version

**Codex terminals:** When a Codex tab ends up sharing one background server with your other Codex tabs, a notice now appears at the top of that tab. On that server, closing one tab can end the others and agent status can be wrong. The notice offers a **Fix** that turns the sharing off and shows the exact command it runs. In a terminal that was opened before the update, it offers to open a new terminal instead. Typing `codex` in a plain fish tab now runs Codex on its own server, as it already did in zsh and bash. Opening a terminal no longer removes Orca's status hook from `~/.codex`. Orca no longer writes a second copy of a folder's trust entry into Codex's `config.toml`, which stopped every `codex` command from working, and it cleans up copies it already wrote. The background Codex usage check no longer clicks "Update now" in Codex's update prompt and leaves Codex broken. Codex also starts without a trust prompt in worktrees of a bare repository. A Codex pane no longer freezes for about a second while you type.

**Folder trust for agents:** When Orca starts Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Qoder, or Antigravity in a folder, it now answers the agent's "Do you trust this folder?" question ahead of time. Orchestration workers, automations, and agents started from your phone no longer get stuck waiting at that prompt. You can turn this off in Settings → Agents → "Trust the folder when Orca starts an agent".

**Agent status:** With several OpenCode 2 panes open, each pane now shows its own Working and Done, not another pane's. On Windows, Claude Code status works again when Claude runs its hooks in Windows PowerShell 5.1. A Codex row stays in the sidebar while Codex runs, even after Codex renames its tab. A freshly started Hermes is shown as ready, not busy.

**Native chat (experimental):** A message you send while the agent is working now waits as a card above the message box, on desktop and on the phone. You can **Steer** it into the running turn, edit it, or delete it. Otherwise it is sent when the turn ends. A subagent's work appears in its own section instead of being mixed into the conversation. `/compact` gets its own row, and an unfinished `/clear` no longer locks the chat. Stop responds faster and no longer shows a false "Cancellation was not confirmed". Pasting text works when you are connected to a remote Orca server.

**Orchestration:** A worker's "I'm done" report is no longer rejected after its conversation is compacted. If Orca is briefly unreachable, the report is retried for about two minutes instead of being lost. `worker-abandon` now settles a stuck worker every time.

**Files and editor:** If you saved a new untitled note and then closed its tab, Orca deleted it. Saved notes are now kept. Clicking in the rich Markdown editor no longer jumps to the top of the file. Open files switch with the system's light and dark mode. Sparse checkouts open the file explorer at the folder you work in.

**Terminal:** Images whose file names have brackets or spaces, like `download (1).png`, now attach to an agent when you drop them in. When dropped files are skipped, the notice tells you why. With many tabs open, the tab you're on stays visible at the edge of the tab bar. Programs like Codex and Claude Code now get the right colors when they start late or in the background.

**Linux and Windows:** On Hyprland, sway, river, and niri, Orca now encrypts saved API keys and tokens when your keyring is running and unlocked. If a credential is saved without encryption, Settings now shows a warning next to it. On Windows, the `orca` command is now a native program, because antivirus kept deleting the old one. It runs without the Visual C++ Redistributable. The installer no longer carries a duplicate copy of Orca's relay files inside the app archive.

**Terminals you already had open:** The new color answers and the `codex` setup in fish tabs take effect in terminals opened after the update. Terminals that were already open keep their old behavior until you open new ones.

## Known issues

**Windows on ARM:** The ARM64 package ships an x64 `orca.exe` command-line tool. Windows 11 on ARM runs it under emulation. Windows 10 on ARM can't run it, so the `orca` command does not work there (#24094).

**OpenCode 2:** OpenCode 2 panes that were already running before the update may show no status until you restart OpenCode in them. If you downgrade Orca after this update, duplicate OpenCode status plugins are left behind. After `opencode run` exits, its pane can keep showing "Done"; a fix is pending in #24472.

**Codex:** After you upgrade, Codex launches use Orca's managed Codex home until Codex approves Orca's new status hook. A resumed pane that uses `~/.codex` can pause for up to 30 seconds (#23552).

**Claude folder trust:** Folder pre-trust is on by default (Settings → Agents → "Trust the folder when Orca starts an agent"). On Alpine WSL, Orca can't copy the file permissions it needs, so Claude shows its own trust prompt instead (#23744).
